items.title: 67460_Sammy Price oral history interview
items.q: But Joe Marsala, his manager, vetoed that.

ctx.x: club. Then I decided, well, what the hell. I went to Ike Levy and asked him to call the Academy of Music and see if they'd let me have the foyer. And a man by the name of Mason who was the manager of the Academy...naturally, Ike Levy called him and he said yes. So then I started having the concerts in the foyer, the foyer of the Academy of Music.

Then I decided that I'd have a big concert. That's when I had Art Tatum and Sidney Bechet. I say that that was the first jazz festival ever held, you know what I mean, in America by a black. And I don't remember anybody else ever having held one before 1947, do you? And then I had Art Tatum, Sidney Bechet, Baby Dodds and Milton Mezzrow and, you know, a lot of people like that. Big, you know what I mean, big flock. Cost me over a thousand dollars, which I had to pay out. Art had promised me that he'd play and if I…

So then I continued to have these festivals, these sessions in the foyer. And then I decided to have a battle of the tenor saxophones, at Town Hall with Lester Young and Zack something and Jimmy Oliver. Was Jimmy Oliver a tenor saxophone player? You remember that name?
